overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the October 12 notices were legible, listed date, time, location and topics, and showed posting date/time. It only encouraged consistency between the Council's page and the official City page.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council posted three notices of its October 12 meeting that were not drafted in an easily understandable format.
allegations.key_passage: The notices were typed in a legible, easily understandable format which listed the date, time and location of the meeting and a list of sufficiently-detailed topics.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the three notices failed to list the meeting time and location.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the notices complied with the Open Meeting Law's notice posting requirements.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notices failed to record the date and time they were posted.
Council's webpage notices differed from the official City notice page (no posting date/time, extra hyperlinks), which may have prompted the complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We encourage the Council to ensure that its meeting notices are consistent both on its own page and on the City's page, which is the official notice posting location.
